ground_truth.description: In ERC-4337, validateUserOp uses external self-call to isValidSignature, changing msg.sender to wallet instead of entrypoint. BaseAuth.signatureValidation enforces caller binding, causing revert for static signatures bound to entrypoint.
ground_truth.root_cause: In ERC-4337, validateUserOp uses external self-call to isValidSignature, changing msg.sender to wallet instead of entrypoint. BaseAuth.signatureValidation enforces caller binding, causing revert for static signatures bound to entrypoint.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Deploy wallet with static signature bound to entrypoint. Attempt validateUserOp → reverts with InvalidStaticSignatureWrongCaller. PoC: Add test to test/modules/ERC4337v07.t.sol: test_validateUserOp_staticSig_callerMismatch_reverts. Uses server and forge test.
ground_truth.fix_description: Avoid external self-call; propagate intended caller into validation.

vulnerabilities.type: DoS due to signature validation failure
vulnerabilities.explanation: The contract uses external self-call `this.isValidSignature(userOpHash, userOp.signature)` which changes msg.sender to the wallet address instead of the entrypoint. BaseAuth.signatureValidation enforces caller binding for static signatures, causing revert when static signatures are bound to the entrypoint address.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Deploy wallet with static signature bound to entrypoint address. 2. User attempts to validate a user operation via EntryPoint. 3. validateUserOp calls isValidSignature via external self-call. 4. BaseAuth.signatureValidation checks if msg.sender (now wallet) matches the bound address (entrypoint). 5. InvalidStaticSignatureWrongCaller revert occurs, preventing validation.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Avoid external self-call by propagating the intended caller into validation. Change line 39 to call an internal function that passes entrypoint as caller parameter, or modify BaseAuth to accept entrypoint as valid caller for ERC-4337 operations.

prediction.overall_explanation: The contract contains a critical design flaw in ERC-4337 signature validation where external self-calls change msg.sender context, causing DoS for wallets using static signatures bound to entrypoint. This prevents legitimate user operations from being validated, breaking core functionality. The vulnerability is clearly documented in the provided benchmark and confirmed by code analysis.
